name: Estonian nationalism
summary: Estonian nationalism seeks the identity, unity, freedom and independence of the Estonian people, rooted in language, culture and a shared homeland. It grew from the 19th-century national awakening, produced the 1918 republic, resisted Soviet occupation and restored the state in 1991. Today it is carried by national-conservative parties that stress Estonian language and citizenship, a self-reliant defence within NATO, restrictive immigration and traditional family policy.
scope: The mainstream ethnocultural nationalism from the national awakening (Jakobson, Koidula) through the 1918 republic, the anti-Soviet resistance and the Singing Revolution, plus its present-day expression in the 1992 constitution's preamble and in the national-conservative parties Isamaa and EKRE. It does not cover Estonian liberal civic patriotism that rejects ethnic framing, nor the most radical fringe. Where Isamaa and EKRE differ (EU, abortion, economics), answers lean to the shared core or are marked low.

sources.usedFor: Mainstream national-conservative party: economic liberalism, Christian democracy, soft Euroscepticism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Isamaa is described as economically liberal, so a mainstream adherent leans pro-market, though EKRE favours a state bank and market development serving national interests.

unions-good.rationale: Estonian nationalism's founding concerns were not labour; adherents are split and sources are silent.

property-fundamental.rationale: The constitution declares property inviolable and equally protected, and national-conservative parties defend it, though limits on land sales to foreigners show it can be overridden for national ends.

regulate-corporations.rationale: EKRE wants markets to serve national interests while Isamaa is economically liberal; adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement's founding project was a parliamentary republic and its restored constitution divides power; Estonia's 1930s authoritarian episode is not a model for the mainstream.

state-harmful.rationale: Estonian nationalism aims to build and maintain a sovereign state; the Singing Revolution restored one.

limit-guns.rationale: EKRE proposed restricting weapons ownership by Russians but the camp also values armed citizen defence; no clear position.

empower-police-military.rationale: EKRE's platform stresses self-reliant defence with conscription, tank battalions and total defence, and the constitution sets a duty to defend the state.

traditional-family.rationale: EKRE ties traditional family models to national survival, and Isamaa shares a family-values line, though only EKRE is cited.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: EKRE opposed the 2014 partnership law and wanted a referendum on marriage; the source covers only that party.

abortion-legal.rationale: EKRE opposes abortion; Isamaa and the wider camp are more mixed, so a moderate disagree.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The constitution's preamble guarantees the preservation of the Estonian people, language and culture, and song festivals are central expressions of the movement.

gradual-change.rationale: Adherents have both cherished institutions and pursued sudden independence; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: EKRE rejects further mass immigration and aims to raise the ethnic Estonian share; Isamaa also takes a restrictive line.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: EKRE wants the EU reformed with national vetoes and less centralisation; nationalists generally resist ceding power to bodies like the UN, while backing NATO.

nation-first.rationale: EKRE frames policy around national survival, but Estonian nationalism also prizes NATO and EU security ties, so views differ.

open-borders.rationale: EKRE opposes immigration and promotes an ethno-state framing, so open borders contradict its stated aims.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Neither the party sources nor the nationalist literature discuss nuclear power, and adherents divide between energy-independence arguments and cost or safety worries.

revolution-justified.rationale: Estonian nationalists regard the 1918 war of independence and the Forest Brethren's armed resistance as legitimate, and the 1991 restoration as justified change.

central-planning.rationale: The Soviet command economy was the occupation regime nationalists fought.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: EKRE favours national-interest markets, Isamaa is economically liberal; split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: EKRE's national public bank hints at state steering while liberals disagree; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Communist abolition of money is the Soviet ideology nationalists opposed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nationalists fought single-party Soviet rule and the Singing Revolution restored multiparty democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Estonia has always been a republic since 1918 and nationalism is bound to it; a hereditary monarch has no place in its tradition.

democracy-best.rationale: The movement founded and restored a democratic republic, but EKRE-style populists distrust some liberal limits, so views differ.

workers-councils.rationale: Soviet-style councils stood for the occupation regime, and the restored republic is built on a parliament, so adherents reject council rule.

right-to-secede.rationale: Estonians claimed the right to leave the USSR; adherents tend to extend self-determination as a principle.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Forest Brethren's armed resistance is honoured while the Singing Revolution was nonviolent, so the tradition is split.

separate-church-state.rationale: The constitution states there is no state church, and nationalism is not tied to religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: No state church and a secular nation identified by language, not religion.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A strong state defence with conscription and constitutional defence duty is the camp's line.

military-superiority.rationale: Estonia seeks deterrence rather than superiority over larger Russia; split.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The constitution's preamble commits the state to preserving the Estonian nation, language and culture, and the movement defines the nation ethnoculturally; the ethno-state wording comes only from EKRE.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation, not class, as the unit; Marxism was the occupier's creed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nationalists prize the Estonian nation-state; ideas of a Nordic identity are cultural, not a political union.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The constitution pairs defence duties with strong rights; adherents split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources are silent; Estonian nationalism has a romantic attachment to the landscape but no stated doctrine on nature's intrinsic worth.

limit-population.rationale: EKRE treats demographic decline as a survival issue and wants more births.

restore-past-order.rationale: The 1991 restoration of the interwar republic is central, but the movement is not anti-progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Nothing in the sources bears on this; the camp prizes pragmatism in economics but firm principle on nation and language.

direct-action.rationale: The Singing Revolution used mass demonstrations but ended in elections and parliament.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Estonian nationalism is a modern state-building project aimed at a sovereign republic, which excludes a return to hunter-gathering.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: This is a Marxist utopian aim; nationalists who fought Soviet communism and defend a market economy reject it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is the communist principle of the Soviet system that nationalists resisted; the market-oriented right prefers earned income.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The exploitation theory of profit is Marxist doctrine, opposed by a nationalism that treats the nation, not class, as the basic unit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Soviet communist dictatorship was the occupation nationalists resisted.

collective-farming.rationale: Soviet collectivisation and terror in Estonia underlie nationalist anti-communism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lenin's imperialism thesis belongs to the ideology that occupied Estonia; adherents attribute wars to empires, not capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Libertarian view is not mainstream among Estonian nationalists, who back the state.

harm-principle.rationale: Economic liberals might agree while social conservatives such as EKRE defend moral limits on conduct, so adherents split.

conscription.rationale: EKRE supports conscription and the constitution establishes the duty to participate in defence.

state-as-business.rationale: The sources give no view; nationalists treat the state as the nation's instrument, not a firm competing for customers.

organic-representation.rationale: Estonia's restored constitution provides representation through a directly elected parliament, not families or trade bodies.

total-state.rationale: Estonian nationalism arose against the totalitarian Soviet state.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The movement seeks to preserve an existing small state; EKRE opposed a border treaty as ceding territory, not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths were the Baltic German order the awakening opposed.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language promotion was central to the awakening; Estonian was never extinct but revival stance generalises.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: EKRE's platform supports a balanced state budget, and Isamaa's economic liberalism points the same way.

rule-by-example.rationale: The constitutional republic rests on written law and elected office, not on rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement seeks freedom, unity and independence of the Estonian people in their own state.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation as the shared community above class, so adherents prefer cooperation to class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving national culture is the movement's central aim, so adherents would not sacrifice inherited institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Estonian nationalists see their security in the Western alliance, not in a front of dominated countries.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: EKRE favours traditional family but Estonia has equal law; split.

ban-interest.rationale: A ban on interest contradicts the market economy that Estonian nationalists built after 1991.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Estonian nationalism is defined by language and culture and the constitution bars discrimination by race, so legal segregation has no place.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The thesis that the state is a ruling-class tool is Marxist, which nationalists oppose; they see the state as the nation's own.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: EKRE favours oil shale for energy independence but sources thin.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: EKRE and the integration policy aim to strengthen Estonian identity and language.

elite-replacement.rationale: Some EKRE leaders voice replacement ideas; mainstream split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about elites being out of touch or general anti-establishment feeling, not about elites putting their own interests first, which this statement now asks.

reviewHistory.rationale: EKRE's populist politics frames established elites as out of touch, a standing theme of the party.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about elites being out of touch or general anti-establishment feeling, not about elites putting their own interests first, which this statement now asks.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

night-watchman-state.rationale: EKRE's active family and demographic policy shows it does not want a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution makes all equal before the law, but adherents draw a national line around citizenship, so the fit is partial.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal debate of Marxist-Leninists; nationalists reject the socialist project entirely.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The constitution guarantees freedom of religion, and the movement is not religiously defined.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle farming is a normal part of Estonian agriculture and no nationalist source proposes a ban.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is Soviet doctrine justifying a strong state; Estonian nationalists opposed that state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 1991 restoration was endorsed by elected bodies and a referendum, and the movement claims legitimacy from the Estonian people.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement stresses national survival and preservation, not social-Darwinian struggle between peoples.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1992 constitution divides power among parliament, president, government and courts, which the movement restored.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined revolutionary vanguard is Leninist doctrine and the model of the occupying party, so nationalists reject it.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: EKRE treats low birth rates as the problem and wants more births, not fewer.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: EKRE frames national survival around ethnic continuity and opposes mass immigration.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Estonia fills offices by election and the movement fought for free elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The constitution allows limited emergency measures; adherents balance security and rights and the sources do not settle it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Soviet control of information was the occupation's method, and the Singing Revolution opposed it.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Soviet system placed the army under the party, which nationalists fought; the constitution makes the army serve the state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: EKRE and Isamaa want stricter citizenship rules including language exams, and EKRE has long sought tighter citizenship law.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: EKRE wants EU reform without centralisation and national vetoes, and Isamaa has run a soft Eurosceptic line, though Estonia is a member.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The constitution gives the president a formal commander role while parliament directs defence; no nationalist source takes a side.

clerical-rule.rationale: The constitution declares there is no state church and the nation is defined by language and culture.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: This is a Leninist slogan, whereas nationalists support national defence and the duty to take part in it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: EKRE supports NATO membership and the movement relies on collective defence against Russia.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Compelling home ownership would contradict a market economy with property rights; no nationalist source proposes it.

people-in-arms.rationale: EKRE favours conscription and total defence rather than abolishing professional forces; the statement mixes both.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Estonians were not divided by an external border in the sense asked, so the sources give no stance.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist EKRE voices such claims, but the movement's founders were teachers and writers, so adherents split.

death-penalty.rationale: Estonia abolished it and adherents are split; the sources discuss no nationalist stance.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Estonia is highly secular and the nationalist parties are not creationist, so teaching it is not on the agenda.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The constitution gives citizenship by birth to children of a citizen parent.

minority-language-support.rationale: EKRE supports shifting Russian-language public schooling to Estonian, and Estonia phased out Russian-medium instruction.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Estonian nationalists see political independence as achieved through the 1991 restoration, with a market economy alongside it.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Estonia's 1992 constitution was drafted by a constitutional assembly and approved by referendum, which the movement treats as the restoration's founding act.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: EKRE prioritises national interests and criticises foreign aid; mainstream adherents are more mixed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Estonia relies on NATO deterrence and EKRE's defence plan builds conventional forces, not nuclear arms.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: EKRE has advocated direct election of the president; the wider camp has not made it a central demand.

central-bank-independence.rationale: EKRE favours a national public bank while liberal adherents accept independence; the sources show a split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: EKRE opposed a border treaty it said would cede Estonian territory, so such trade-offs are rejected.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The constitution protects property but permits expropriation for the public interest; adherents are split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The sources do not engage the Marxist debate; Estonian nationalists simply call the USSR an occupying totalitarian state.

collective-defense.rationale: EKRE backs NATO membership within a self-reliant defence policy, and a small nation facing Russia relies on Article 5 style mutual defence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Estonians hold that the 1940 annexation was an unlawful occupation, restored in 1991.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Estonian nationalists favour a unitary state with one legal system; the idea comes from other contexts.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Estonia is a republic and nationalism rests on the people, not on a sacred head of state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Estonia's economically liberal right introduced flat tax in 1994.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The constitution binds all offices to law and nationalists fought arbitrary Soviet rule.

leader-cult.rationale: Cults of personality belong to the Soviet era that nationalists denounce; the republic's culture is not centred on a leader.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis about socialist societies, rejected by a nationalism opposed to socialism itself.

land-redistribution.rationale: Soviet and post-1919 reforms; restitution after 1991 instead.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: EKRE claims the territory Estonia lost in 1920 treaty adjustments only as border.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The constitution guarantees freedom of religion, and nationalism here is not religiously defined.

women-must-cover.rationale: No nationalist source proposes dress mandates and the constitution protects personal freedom and equality.

common-currency.rationale: Estonia uses the euro and Isamaa is pro-European while EKRE criticises the EU, so adherents split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Finnic kinship and Nordic identity discussed in nationalist discourse are cultural, not a call for political union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Nationalists back national cultural institutions such as song festivals; this tradition of cultural self-government is accepted but not detailed in sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalism treats nations, culture and will as the drivers of history, in opposition to historical materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: No stated position; liberal economists might support competition law while nationalists prefer national champions.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Populist EKRE criticises limits on majorities while the constitution and Isamaa back constitutional courts; adherents split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Economic nationalism in EKRE leans this way but Estonia is a small open economy; split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives with moral ones is a Soviet-era slogan that nationalists reject.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Forest Brethren fought as a guerrilla movement, but a foco theory of revolution is not part of nationalist doctrine.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The awakening opposed the privileges of the Baltic German nobility and the republic is built on equal citizens.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The awakening and song festivals promote national history and identity as the core of Estonian schooling and culture.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Estonians experienced rule by outsiders (Baltic Germans, Russians, Soviets) and claim self-rule, so they reject tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: EKRE and the integration policy stress pride in Estonian identity and statehood, schools included.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Economically liberal wing assumes markets endure; nothing in sources on crisis theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Estonians themselves were a subject of imperial rule and resist Russian influence over them.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Leninist argument that nationalists would not adopt.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Economic liberals might agree, social nationalists mixed; adherents split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1992 constitution has a rights chapter that is hard to amend and the movement built it.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The Molotov-Ribbentrop pact that carved up the Baltics is held void, the core of the 1987 Hirvepark protest.

elective-rulers.rationale: Estonia has an elected parliament and a president chosen by parliament or electors.

minority-veto.rationale: Nationalists seek decisions by the national majority, and no minority veto exists in the constitution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The constitution gives the Riigikogu the central lawmaking role.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Estonian nationalism is a mobilising movement, from the awakening to the Singing Revolution, not a call to withdraw.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not a nationalist theme; Estonian nationalism sees mass culture such as the song festival as a source of strength.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The Gramscian explanation is not used by adherents, who would credit coercion in the Soviet case.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is alien to a movement that joined the West.

native-born-offices.rationale: EKRE said loyalty of non-Estonians in officer posts could not be assumed; citizenship-based office limits suit the camp.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-internal question; nationalists reject communism wholesale.

return-lost-territory.rationale: EKRE opposed a border treaty as ceding Estonian territory beyond the Narva and Petseri lines, so would not drop such a claim.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Estonian nationalists define themselves by anti-communism and resist Soviet-style anti-fascist rhetoric.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Estonian nationalism holds Soviet and Nazi occupations both as crimes; the 1987 demonstrations demanded condemnation of the pact.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: This American historical question has no link to Estonian nationalism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Estonia removed Soviet monuments; nationalists back removal.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Estonians seek Western institutions and reject Eurasian alternatives.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The armed forces are defenders under civilian control in the constitution; a political guardian role is not claimed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The constitution gives members of parliament a free mandate, and nationalists work within it.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Estonia's second pillar is private accounts, supported by liberal right.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The constitution calls property inviolable, and Estonia restored private land ownership after 1991.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The constitution gives the Riigikogu authority over the state budget, which the restored republic upholds.

single-official-language.rationale: Article 6 states the official language of Estonia is Estonian and Article 52 makes it the language of state bodies.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: EKRE wants limits on land sales to foreigners; the wider camp is more moderate.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Soviet invasion of 1940 and later is the nationalist cause for resistance.

corporate-influence.rationale: Populist concerns about lobbies coexist with liberal economics, so adherents split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: EKRE-style nationalists attempt to limit foreign-funded NGOs.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: EKRE proposes per-child mortgage relief and tax cuts for parents to reverse population decline; the source covers only that party.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Nationalists value the restored constitutional order and defend its authority.

non-intervention.rationale: Estonians invoke non-interference for themselves but accept responses to Russia.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Fringe nationalists voice such claims, but the movement's mainstream sources do not, so adherents split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: EKRE champions marriage and traditional family models as the base of the nation, so abolishing it is rejected.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Estonia's constitution guarantees access to information held by authorities.

informal-organisation.rationale: Estonian nationalism built formal parties, societies and state institutions, though the Singing Revolution was informal.

national-law-over-international.rationale: EKRE wants national vetoes in the EU; Estonian constitutional law is primary.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by language and culture, with no state church.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Refusing deference to Moscow, from independence in 1918 to the Singing Revolution, is the core of the movement.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The constitution protects every person's property, which includes belongings; the Marxist framing is not used.

defeat-communism.rationale: The movement fought Soviet communism through the Forest Brethren and the Singing Revolution.

religion-illusion.rationale: Estonian nationalists are not committed to this Marxist claim, though many are personally secular.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The post-1991 right built a market economy and credits it with growth, though the Marxist phrasing is not theirs.

socialized-care.rationale: EKRE stresses family responsibility for raising children over collective care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism has strands in Estonian history but mainstream is split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Reorganising society into cooperative communes is not a nationalist aim.

majority-settlement.rationale: Nothing in the sources endorses settling majority members in minority regions; EKRE's stance is on immigration and language.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Estonian right accepts the market economy while rejecting communism, so a third way is not its program.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Nationalism rests on a shared homeland and ancestral memory, which supports weighing historical ties to land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial is not part of mainstream Estonian nationalism, which sources frame around independence and culture.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: EKRE opposes partnership law but no stated call to criminalise.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Singing Revolution and the restored republic were fought against suppression of independent organisations.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The constitution protects religious freedom and the nation is not religiously defined.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Estonians experienced exploitation under imperial and Soviet rule and reject colonial economics.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The concept belongs to Islamic law and has no role in nationalist doctrine; adherents are indifferent or dismissive.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The movement is secular in basis, and the constitution has no religious test for rulers.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: EKRE and conservative nationalists oppose identity-politics frameworks of this kind.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: EKRE opposes this legal recognition and favours traditional family and gender norms.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept that nationalists do not use.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The constitution says power comes from the people and the movement is secular in basis, though Isamaa has Christian-democratic roots.

social-market-economy.rationale: Isamaa is economically liberal while family-support policies of EKRE involve state protections; adherents split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: EKRE's platform builds conscription, tank battalions and total defence, and the constitution requires participation in defence.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: EKRE supports NATO membership and Estonian nationalism seeks alliance protection against Russia.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Estonia is a republic with elected heads of state and nationalist doctrine has no dynastic element.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit banking is not part of the mainstream program; EKRE's national bank is a different idea.

property-franchise.rationale: The constitution gives the vote to every adult citizen regardless of property, and nationalists seek to restrict by citizenship, not wealth.

domination-women-nature.rationale: This ecofeminist thesis is opposed by traditional-family nationalism.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept not used by nationalists.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A Marxist critique that the liberal-market right does not share.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The constitution requires laws to be published and binds officials to them, which the restored republic embodies.

racial-franchise.rationale: Estonia's franchise rests on citizenship, though nationalists favour restricting non-citizen voting; no racial franchise is proposed.

online-participation.rationale: Estonia is a digital state but sources on nationalism do not discuss online deliberation.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The constitution protects religious freedom, and nationalists define the nation by language, not faith.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotts of minority-owned shops are not part of mainstream Estonian nationalism, which sources frame around language and culture.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Soviet promotion of atheism was part of the occupation regime that nationalists opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nationalists back strong defence and law enforcement; abolition is outside the camp's thinking.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Estonian nationalists seek Estonian-language majority governance, not guaranteed shares of power for communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The liberal wing leans toward charity while pronatalist EKRE favours state family aid; adherents split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not a nationalist theme, and the constitution has parliamentary representation.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Search coverage reports that EKRE and Isamaa both want to restrict voting rights of non-Estonian, non-EU residents, so allowing foreign residents to vote locally is opposed.

abolish-ip.rationale: The constitution protects property including intellectual property, and nationalists have no stated case to abolish it.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Estonia has defence-minded youth organisations, but the sources do not take a nationalist position on them.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: EKRE supports NATO membership and allied presence, so hosting foreign forces is accepted.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Estonians seek recognition of Soviet deportations as genocide.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Estonian nationalism honours armed defence of the nation, so pacifism of this kind is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Nationalism rests on ancestral myths and legal continuity of the 1918 republic.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: EKRE's traditional stance on sex and gender rejects this.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Estonian nationalism is secular in basis and frames politics around national survival.

culture-before-state.rationale: The national awakening built culture, language and press before independence in 1918.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: EKRE's restrictions on foreign land, interest in national control.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Estonia is a single state of its people so the question does not arise.

independent-unions.rationale: Independent unions follow from rejecting Soviet state control, though labour is a minor theme for the movement.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist debate that nationalists do not take part in.

second-chamber.rationale: Estonia's Riigikogu is unicameral and nationalist parties do not call for a second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Private property is protected by the constitution, and the movement does not endorse community ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: A unitary-state nationalism does not favour confederations of municipalities.

anonymous-payments.rationale: No nationalist source covers private digital payments, and security-minded and liberty-minded adherents would diverge.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Estonia is a unitary state with local governments under national law; nationalists accept this.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Estonian nationalism is based on language and culture, not race, though EKRE speaks of ethnic continuity.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Estonia's defence is built on territorial self-defence and NATO's collective defence, with no aggressive aims.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The constitution's preamble ties people and language; Estonian nationalism arose on language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Estonia has one electorate of citizens, and nationalists restrict rather than separate voting rolls by community.

future-generations.rationale: Constitution preamble speaks of preservation through the ages.

arms-reduction.rationale: EKRE plans more tanks and air defence, and the movement stresses military readiness against Russia.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secret protocols are condemned; thus generally pro-openness.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Estonia keeps a voluntary citizen Defence League, and nationalists support armed citizen defence.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Nationalists back the constitutional duty to take part in national defence and military service.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: EKRE supports a balanced budget and Isamaa is fiscally liberal, so binding limits on borrowing fit.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Estonian nationalists integrated into the Western economy and do not call for restructuring it for developing states.

smash-state-machine.rationale: A Leninist doctrine; nationalists want to build and keep the Estonian state.

sacred-nation.rationale: The song festival and national awakening treat the nation as an enduring community, with quasi-sacred ritual.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not a nationalist theme; adherents focus on external domination.

public-service-media.rationale: Estonia maintains a public broadcaster; nationalists accept it though EKRE has criticised its coverage.

workers-own-party.rationale: The nationalist view treats the nation, not class, as the base of politics.

ban-fgm.rationale: The constitution guarantees equality and bodily integrity, and nationalists do not defend the practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal rights before the law, including property, are in the constitution; nationalism does not contest them.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Estonia has no customary chiefs and law-making belongs to parliament under the constitution.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: EKRE requires high-level Estonian from teachers and Estonian-language citizenship exams are a long-standing demand of the camp; extending it to immigrants generally follows.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The constitution protects all religions equally and there is no state church.

women-suffrage.rationale: The constitution's Article 57 gives every adult citizen the vote without distinction by sex, and the nationalist parties do not contest it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not a nationalist claim; the movement does not blame religion for women's status.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The movement was built on resisting Soviet occupation and its planned economy.

national-church-status.rationale: The constitution gives no church special status, and the national movement is largely secular.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Colonial borders are not directly relevant; the movement stresses historical borders of its own state.

simple-living.rationale: Isamaa and EKRE do not make simple living a theme; adherents are indifferent.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The constitution's preamble commits the state to preserve the Estonian nation and culture through the ages, and the movement ties identity to the ancestral homeland.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The constitution guarantees the right to life and due process, and no Estonian nationalist party calls for killing suspects without trial.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Family-policy emphasis favours broad benefits while fiscal conservatives favour targeting; adherents split and sources do not settle it.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Estonian nationalism works through parties (Isamaa, EKRE) in a parliamentary republic and has not sought to bypass them.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The constitution separates church and state and Estonian nationalism is ethnolinguistic rather than denominational.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The constitution guarantees equality before the law and Estonian family law lets either spouse seek divorce; the nationalist parties do not contest this.

national-resource-control.rationale: The constitution declares Estonian natural resources national wealth to be used sparingly, reflecting national control over them.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The constitution rests on rights while sovereignty-minded parties stress positive law; adherents are not clearly split either way in sources.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The movement is built on resisting Soviet occupation and communist rule, restored in 1991, so communist-party leadership is rejected.

missingStatements.text: A state may require non-citizens to pass a language test in the national language before they can become citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: EKRE and Isamaa seek Estonian-language examinations for citizenship, and the constitution makes Estonian the official language.

missingStatements.text: Non-citizen residents should not be allowed to vote in elections.
missingStatements.rationale: EKRE and Isamaa want to restrict voting rights of non-Estonian, non-EU residents, tying the vote to the national community.

notes: Isamaa (Christian-democratic, economically liberal, soft Eurosceptic) and EKRE (ethno-state framing, anti-immigration, abortion opponent) diverge on economics, EU reform and social issues; many economic answers are low confidence for that reason. Sources are Wikipedia-heavy; the constitution is the only primary text opened.
